issues.title: [Web UX] Deliver a self-explanatory ADORE operator interface
issues.files: Cross-component delivery; this issue coordinates the child issues.
issues.spec:
## Problem and target behaviour
The current dashboard exposes configuration and orchestration concepts before explaining the user's task. The redesigned interface must let a person unfamiliar with ADORE and AEGIS understand projects, jobs, waiting states, configuration changes and consumption without verbal training.

Keep the useful Overview direction. Use a dark #102F29 navigation panel, neutral content surfaces, green action accents and the approved transparent DDP Engineering mark in muted sage #B8D1C4, without a white logo panel. Keep company branding separate from the ADORE product name. The reference prototype is illustrative, not production code.

## Delivery scope
- Clear navigation: Overview, Projects, Jobs, Statistics; administrator-only Users, Change history and System status; account/preferences remain accessible.
- Guided new enrollment and exact host-specific TOML enrollment; new projects begin with pickup stopped.
- Portable settings export/import and copying settings to a new project.
- Project hub, globally scoped jobs, evidence-based waiting reasons and next actions.
- Purpose-based configuration and candidate before/after review.
- Consistent project/period/timezone statistics, per-job consumption and honest measurement coverage.
- Explicit message definitions and source capabilities before message collection.
- Admin/dev accounts with project-scoped developer access and structured redacted audit history.
- Keyboard, responsive, light/dark theme and novice-user acceptance verification.

## Shared product boundaries
ADORE may publish draft MR/PRs and never merges. Approval remains on the forge and bound to the current validated candidate. Project pickup stopped does not pause an active job. Preserve forge/executor/runtime independence, server-side RBAC, admin-only financial data, CSRF, revision checks, lock/idle requirements and fail-closed corrupt-input handling.
The backend role remains developer; the UI may call it Dev. Unknown measurements are not zero. No live forge calls on every page refresh, fabricated progress percentages, browser secrets, automatic repository cloning or email invitation system.

## Priority and release policy
P1: core clarity, safe enrollment, operational flows and final acceptance gate. P2: complete the configuration portability, statistics and administration capabilities. Priority does not override dependencies.
The backlog is not an authorization to start autonomous execution. Before pickup, verify blockers, remove agent-hold where appropriate and let the operator explicitly apply the configured ready label. Native Gitea dependencies must also be checked; do not assume ADORE enforces them.

## Dependency graph and rollout
{{CHILD_TABLE}}

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All child deliverables and their negative trust-boundary tests pass; no blocked implementation is claimed complete.
- [ ] Every public mutation explains its effect, shows a meaningful result and enforces authorization on the server.
- [ ] Novice acceptance evidence meets the final verification issue's targets, or a human records the actual shortfall and remediation.
- [ ] No merge button, arbitrary job pause/resume, fabricated message count or all-time card mislabeled as period data.
- [ ] Operator and component documentation, changelog and applicable AEGIS knowledge reflect the delivered behaviour.
- [ ] The baseline and approved asset bundle are available remotely before child implementation starts.

## Baseline and design assets
Inspected local branch: task/adore-web-interface at 6fed00c. Remote branch was 450798e when this backlog was prepared; bootstrap must publish/reconcile the validation tooling commit before implementation. Do not use master as an equivalent web baseline.
The approved local design history is 00_Planning/2026-10-05_Web_UX_Redesign/. A portable reference archive is attached to this epic when available; its English README and the issue requirements are authoritative for implementation. Historical screenshots may contain Romanian copy; all new tickets, implementation specs and documentation are English.
No release version or deadline is assigned by this epic.

## Problem and target behaviour
The current application mixes broad navigation, technical terms and inconsistent visual scope. Introduce the shared shell and reusable presentation primitives that later flows consume.

## Scope
Keep React/TypeScript/Vite and existing route semantics. Extract page-level components incrementally, without a wholesale framework replacement. Implement Overview/Projects/Jobs/Statistics navigation; contextual project subnavigation; admin navigation and account/preferences. Use clear headings, visible scope, one main contextual action, accessible status labels and progressive disclosure.
Integrate the approved DDP Engineering transparent sage mark on the dark navigation background without a white rectangle; preserve the custom logo proportions. ADORE remains the product label. The source asset must come from the bootstrap reference bundle.
Define English copy for job, enrolled project, pickup stopped, waiting for clarification, waiting for approval and draft review. Preserve supported localization catalogs and theme preferences; do not copy hardcoded Romanian prototype text into production.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Main routes and browser Back/deep links continue to work; project context is visible and preserved deliberately.
- [ ] Admin and Dev navigation reflect their server-authorized capabilities; a Dev with no grants gets a useful empty state.
- [ ] The logo has no pale backing panel and scales without distortion at desktop and 390px width; both themes remain readable.
- [ ] State is conveyed with text/icon as well as colour; essential field instructions are visible, not placeholder-only.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation, visible focus and semantic headings work across shell navigation.
- [ ] Loading, no records and failed requests have different presentations; failed requests do not show false zero totals.
- [ ] No new UI control promises an unsupported approval, merge, clone or job pause operation.

## Verification
Frontend helper/type/build checks plus offline browser navigation, roles, missing-data/error, both-theme and narrow-viewport scenarios. Preserve existing route/i18n regression coverage. Inspect representative screenshots; do not claim full WCAG compliance from automated checks alone.

issues.title: [Web UX] Add stable display identity and safe paused-enrollment backend contracts
issues.files: 04_Software/adore/profiles.py, wizard.py, web/app.py, web/store.py and command boundaries where necessary; test_profiles.py, test_web_projects.py, test_web_readiness.py; Component_Profiles, Component_Wizard and Component_Web_API docs.
issues.spec:
## Problem and target behaviour
The current project name is an immutable restricted profile ID, not a human display name. Exact TOML imports pause pickup, but the web new-project flow must guarantee the same safe state before exposing the profile to workers.

## Scope and contract decisions
Add a human display_name separate from the stable existing profile ID. Existing profiles use the ID as their display fallback. Never rename profile directories, state roots, memberships, operation ownership or URLs when display_name changes. Provide server-side deterministic ID validation/availability; an automatically suggested slug still requires collision checking.
Guarantee all web-created projects start with pickup stopped atomically with respect to worker discovery. Existing running projects and unrelated CLI enrollment behaviour remain unchanged unless separately specified.
Return structured setup validation with stable code, field/path and human-readable remediation. Separate structural validity, pickup state and last explicit environment verification. Reuse explicit readiness commands and protect their results against stale configuration revisions. No automatic network/container probes while typing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New valid web enrollment returns a stable ID, display name and pickup-stopped state; the worker cannot observe an intermediate pickup-active project.
- [ ] Existing profiles load with the display fallback and unchanged permissions/paths; corrupt metadata is rejected, not reset.
- [ ] Duplicate/reserved/malformed IDs, invalid display input, invalid setup and concurrent creation fail with typed errors and no orphaned runnable profile.
- [ ] Activating pickup remains an explicit authorized operation; pause never claims to stop active jobs.
- [ ] A readiness result identifies the checked configuration revision and time; stale/unverified is distinct from invalid.
- [ ] Admin mutation/CSRF guards apply; Dev cannot create or change identity through direct API requests.
- [ ] Setup never accepts secret values in place of supported credential references.

## Verification
Happy path and negative tests at profile/config/worker boundaries, including concurrent visibility and rollback. Fake all forge/runtime commands. Cover stable-ID behaviour across memberships, operations and existing serialized profile fixtures; document any storage compatibility change without silently changing runtime state schema 1.

issues.title: [Web UX] Build guided project enrollment with explicit verification and review
issues.files: Frontend enrollment page/components, API types, i18n and route handling; existing POST /projects and readiness contracts; browser fixtures; Component_Web_Frontend and operator setup guidance.
issues.spec:
## Problem and target behaviour
The current enrollment form presents infrastructure fields together without explaining what the user is creating. Introduce a six-step task-based flow with visible instructions and a final review.

## Scope
Steps: method -> repository/identity -> working environment -> eligibility/reviewers/limits -> verification -> review/create. Initially expose only implemented methods; portable settings and clone options become active with their delivering issue.
Explain that the local clone folder is on the ADORE server and must already contain the repository. Require actual supported platform, owner/repo identifier, branch, executor/provider/model, runtime/image and authentication reference. Do not implement automatic repository cloning or accept unsupported URL parsing.
Start with honest explicit environment choices. Offer presets only if a real validated inventory exists; do not invent installed images or providers. Advanced options expose existing supported configuration. Structural validation is separate from an explicitly initiated environment probe, with an effect summary before the probe.
Keep the draft in memory, preserve Back/correction values and warn on navigation loss. No durable draft API or localStorage secrets in this scope.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Visible instructions explain every mandatory concept without requiring prior AEGIS/ADORE knowledge.
- [ ] Back and review Change links retain entries; changing upstream choices invalidates dependent checks.
- [ ] Field and summary errors point to the corrective step and move focus accessibly.
- [ ] An explicit review lists identity, repository, environment, rules/limits, reviewers and server locations.
- [ ] Confirmation submits exactly the reviewed draft/revision and prevents accidental double creation.
- [ ] Completion states that pickup is stopped; activation is a separate explicit action and does not promise a specific ticket will start.
- [ ] Invalid configuration blocks creation; readiness failure is explained with a recheck action and cannot be hidden behind a successful badge.
- [ ] No secrets, browser-machine paths masquerading as server paths, fake presets or disabled-feature promises.

## Verification
Offline E2E valid enrollment, empty/malformed fields, ID collision, invalid clone/runtime, failed/stale readiness, changed upstream choice, back/review correction, double submit, Dev denial and refresh/navigation-loss scenarios. Verify keyboard/focus and 390px layout.

## Problem and target behaviour
Current job listings are project-scoped and the compact view omits ticket titles and detailed waiting evidence. A global UI must not concatenate incomplete per-project pages or infer actions from a stage label.

## Scope
Provide server-authorized global/project job listing with deterministic pagination, search and simple status groups. Identity is (project_id, run_id); identical run IDs in two projects must not collide.
Expose lifecycle, exact AEGIS stage, outcome, persisted last activity, safe ticket/MR URL and available ticket title, wait reason, responsible role/person and evidence location. Do not invent titles, questions, named reviewers or outcomes. Old jobs without new metadata use honest fallbacks.
Prefer persisted snapshots/read models; no forge fetch per refresh. Add optional evidence only with an explicit compatibility analysis of schema-1 state/journals; never reset old/corrupt state.

- [ ] Unsafe/malformed URLs and corrupt persisted input fail closed without secret leakage.

issues.files: adore/metrics.py, web/app.py usage/metrics/export views, run/journal projections; test_metrics.py, test_web_metrics.py, test_web_pricing.py; Component_Metrics/Web_API docs.
issues.spec:
## Problem and target behaviour
All-time totals and period aggregates coexist under date controls, and absent consumption can look like zero. Establish one explicit scope for every measure and export.

## Scope and metric definitions
Scope is authorized project set + interval + IANA timezone + granularity. Use a documented half-open instant interval [from,to), with date controls translated to local-midnight boundaries; handle DST correctly.
Started/completed/failed counts use their own lifecycle event times. Active now is a separate current-state stock. Token/cost totals are attributed by event consumption time, not job start time. Per-job lifetime and in-period consumption are distinct fields identified by (project_id,run_id).
Unknown/unreported tokens or cost are null/unavailable with coverage, not measured zero. Reported and estimated costs remain separate and admin-only. Missing/invalid timestamps are counted as unallocated, never guessed into a date bucket. Rates/durations expose denominator/sample definitions.
Reuse compatible existing aggregates, add the missing contract and filtered CSV semantics. Do not migrate/reset runtime state or relabel executor launches as messages.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All scoped cards, tables, charts and CSV use the same project/period/timezone definitions; all-time is an explicit scope.
- [ ] Cross-period jobs contribute consumption to each actual event period and lifecycle counts to their own event timestamps.
- [ ] All missing data, measured zero, unavailable date attribution and failed load are distinguishable.
- [ ] Cost redaction holds on every admin/developer endpoint/export, including new per-job projections.
- [ ] Replay/deduplication, same run ID in two projects, boundary dates and DST do not double count or leak scopes.
- [ ] Invalid filters/timezones/ranges, corrupt timestamps/events and unknown persisted schema fail with typed errors.
- [ ] Rates and mean/median durations match documented samples rather than approximate browser filtering.
- [ ] Current-stock values are not mislabeled period totals.

## Verification
Offline analytical fixtures with hand-calculated expected counts/tokens, cross-midnight/DST, interval boundaries, missing timestamps, absent versus zero usage, replay, costs, CSV and RBAC negatives. Include source-coverage assertions and preserve price-history semantics.

Provide an atomic create-user-with-grants server operation while preserving existing APIs where compatible. Validate project existence/visibility and race conditions on the server; rollback on failure. Access editing shows before/after and result.
Retain password hashing, session/CSRF protections, last-admin safety and disabled-user rules. Display names never substitute for grant identities.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Valid admin/dev creation assigns exactly the reviewed privileges and grants atomically.
- [ ] Invalid/duplicate username, invalid role/password, unknown/archived or concurrently deleted project and invalid grants reject without partial user creation.
- [ ] Selecting admin makes all-project access explicit; Dev with no projects is an explicit reviewed choice rather than accidental success.

issues.title: [Web UX] Verify the integrated redesign with offline regression and novice-user acceptance
issues.files: 04_Software/web/e2e and helper tests; relevant 04_Software/tests/test_web_*; accessibility checks; English acceptance report/operator walkthrough; component docs and CHANGELOG.md.
issues.spec:
## Problem and target behaviour
A guided interface is not proven self-explanatory by a mockup or green unit suite. Validate the integrated product and record actual novice-user findings before closing the epic.

## Scope
Add meaningful offline E2E scenarios across enrollment, exact/portable import, cloning, blocked/stale settings review, all job waiting/result states, statistics scope/coverage, user grants and audit. Reuse isolated fake-boundary server/worker; no real forge/docker/git/executor commands in tests.
Verify keyboard/focus, field errors/status announcements, light/dark contrasts, responsive reflow at 390px, readable charts/tables and direct links. Target WCAG 2.2 AA; record manual gaps instead of claiming certification from tooling.
Conduct observed acceptance tasks with five people unfamiliar with ADORE/AEGIS, in a safe prepared environment. The implementation agent can prepare the session and fixtures but must not invent participants, timings, approvals or findings. Owner arranges unavailable human sessions; report the gate as pending until genuine evidence exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Full offline Python and frontend validation passes; meaningful negative trust boundaries are covered and existing contracts preserved.
- [ ] At least 4/5 participants explain pickup stopped versus waiting for clarification within one minute without coaching.
- [ ] At least 4/5 enroll a prepared-environment project within ten minutes without verbal instruction; infrastructure setup time is separate.
- [ ] At least 4/5 identify where candidate approval happens and understand ADORE never merges.
- [ ] At least 4/5 identify portable import inclusions/exclusions and required target values.
- [ ] Every participant can inspect the proposed change before apply and return to correct an enrollment choice.
- [ ] Project/period/timezone changes consistently scope cards, charts, tables and export; unavailable data differs from zero.
- [ ] Dev cannot bypass project restrictions or access financial/admin features through direct routes/API/export.
- [ ] Findings and unresolved accessibility/usability gaps have reproduction/evidence and follow-up ownership; no fabricated acceptance success.

## Verification and delivery
Run the repository's required AEGIS validation plus documented pytest/Ruff/frontend type/build/helper/E2E checks. Use the agreed release-candidate baseline, deterministic fixtures and manual keyboard/screen-reader/contrast inspection where needed. Live acceptance probes remain operator-authorized.
Deliver an English report of observed results and limitations, final operator guidance and changelog. Publication is draft-only and human-approved. If human evaluation is unavailable, finish technical evidence but keep the human acceptance/epic gate open.
